correctness.rationale: For a binary law relabeled so p<=q, the centered information content is exactly the two-point mean-zero variable taking q log(q/p) with probability p and -p log(q/p) with probability q. Its stop-loss transform is explicit. Comparing it piecewise with the stop-loss transform of Exp(1)-1 reduces the only nontrivial interval to maximizing p(qd-a)e^(1+a). If d>=1 the maximum is p^p q^q<=1; if d<1 it is pd e^(1-pd)<=1, using pd<=p log(1/p)<=1/e. Equal means plus all-threshold stop-loss domination proves convex order. The MGF corollary follows by the convex test exp(tx).

originality.rationale: The novelty claim is the full convex-order domination of centered binary information content by Exp(1)-1. The already-known gamma/exponential MGF inequality is explicitly treated as prior coverage. Bhatt--Pensia establish centered relative-entropy concentration; Agrawal states the sharper gamma-MGF conjecture; Melbourne--Palafox-Castillo already prove the unit-gamma MGF information-content bound for monotone log-concave discrete laws, which includes Bernoulli. Full-text inspection of the latter's information-concentration section and convex-order appendix found no centered-information-content convex-order theorem. Targeted published-record and public-literature searches likewise found no equivalent binary shifted-exponential convex-order statement.
residual_risks: An equivalent binary stop-loss or convex-order statement may exist in older stochastic-order or information-theory literature under terminology not retrieved by the bounded searches.

value.rationale: The result upgrades a natural sharp benchmark in centered relative-entropy concentration from one family of exponential tests to the complete convex stochastic order in the smallest nontrivial empirical problem. Convex order simultaneously controls every stop-loss functional and every convex loss, so the theorem exposes distributional structure that the known MGF bound does not. The binary one-sample case is a canonical base object in the literature's alphabet-reduction arguments, making the strengthening mathematically motivated rather than an arbitrary slice.
